changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For operations owners at high-stakes event buyers: 'A name, not a queue. A named solutions engineer and account lead, a shared channel, and someone who picks up on on-sale morning.' Lead with who answers when it breaks, not with tiers or response times.
changes.why: The decider dismissed our tiered support as 'a queue with a faster timer' and chose the vendor that offered named people and an on-call promise, in the words 'a name, not a queue' and 'someone who picks up'.

changes.change: Add an on-sale readiness plan as a proof point for ticketing and event buyers: a one-page, on-paper plan of what we do on an on-sale morning (who is on call, how the shared channel works, what happens at minute four if payments fail), paired with a named ticketing reference who can say who picked up. Offer it in the first meeting with the operations owner.
changes.why: The decider asked to see on paper what we do on an on-sale morning, we had no such asset, and the rep admits it was buildable but offered logos instead.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For event and ticketing buyers, replace generic logos and stories with a named reference: 'Talk to [name] at [ticketing customer] about who picked up on their on-sale morning.' Put a person, not a logo wall, in front of the operations owner.
changes.why: The rep says 'I had logos. I didn't have a person', and the customer's language was about someone who picks up, which logos do not answer.

changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: Stop leading with the developer and sandbox or load-test story when the economic decider is an operations owner. Keep it for the technical evaluator, and for the COO use: 'I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down.' Answer what happens when it's down first.
changes.why: The load test won the CTO but drew only 'good.' from the decider, who said she does not buy uptime but what happens when it is down.
